hello-world.title: Print text to standard output
hello-world.summary: Write one line with System.out.println. Available on Java 8 and later.
hello-world.why: Standard output is the simplest way to verify program behavior, and println also appends a line break.
hello-world.tips: Use print when you do not want a newline, and printf when you need formatted output.

main-method.title: The main method
main-method.short: Understand the Java application entry point
main-method.summary: Understand the Java application entry point. Available on Java 8 and later.
main-method.why: A normal Java application starts when the JVM finds a main method with the expected signature.
main-method.tips: Treat public, static, void, and String[] as separate parts of the contract when debugging startup problems.

var-local-inference.title: Local variable type inference with var
var-local-inference.short: Infer a local variable type from its initializer
var-local-inference.summary: Infer a local variable type from its initializer. Available on Java 10 and later.
var-local-inference.why: var is still statically typed: the compiler determines a concrete type from the initializer at compile time.
var-local-inference.tips: Use an explicit type when inference hurts readability, and remember that var is not allowed for fields or method parameters.

switch-expression.title: Return a value from a switch expression
switch-expression.summary: Use switch as an expression. Available on Java 14 and later.
switch-expression.why: A switch expression can return a value directly, reducing temporary assignments and accidental fall-through.
switch-expression.tips: Use yield for multi-statement arms and check that enum or sealed-type cases are covered as intended.

text-block.title: Multiline strings with text blocks
text-block.short: Write multiline strings with triple quotes
text-block.summary: Write multiline strings with triple quotes. Available on Java 15 and later.
text-block.why: Text blocks make JSON, SQL, and other multiline text readable without heavy escaping.
text-block.tips: Check leading and trailing newlines and indentation stripping rules when exact whitespace matters.

record-type.title: Create data carriers with records
record-type.summary: Declare compact data-carrier classes. Available on Java 16 and later.
record-type.why: Records generate accessors, equals, hashCode, and toString from their components, making value-oriented data types concise.
record-type.tips: Record components are final references, but objects referenced by those components are not automatically deeply immutable.

sealed-classes.title: Restrict inheritance with sealed classes
sealed-classes.short: Limit which types may extend or implement a type
sealed-classes.summary: Limit which types may extend or implement a type. Available on Java 17 and later.
sealed-classes.why: A sealed hierarchy prevents unexpected subtypes and makes closed-domain pattern handling easier to reason about.
sealed-classes.tips: Each permitted subtype must be final, sealed, or non-sealed, so decide the extension policy for the whole hierarchy.

virtual-threads.title: Use virtual threads
virtual-threads.short: Run many blocking tasks on lightweight threads
virtual-threads.summary: Run many blocking tasks on lightweight threads. Available on Java 21 and later.
virtual-threads.why: Virtual threads make large numbers of blocking tasks practical without requiring the same number of platform threads.
virtual-threads.tips: They do not make CPU-bound work faster; also watch for contention and operations that pin carrier threads for long periods.

primitive-vs-reference.title: Primitive and reference types
primitive-vs-reference.short: Distinguish primitive values from object references
primitive-vs-reference.summary: Distinguish primitive values from object references. Available on Java 8 and later.
primitive-vs-reference.why: This distinction affects assignment, nullability, equality, boxing, and how values are passed around.
primitive-vs-reference.tips: Pay special attention when wrapper types are auto-boxed because null and == can behave differently from primitives.

string-immutability.title: String is immutable
string-immutability.short: Understand that String operations create new strings
string-immutability.summary: Understand that String operations create new strings. Available on Java 8 and later.
string-immutability.why: A String never changes after creation, so concatenation and replacement return new String objects.
string-immutability.tips: Use StringBuilder for heavy loop-based concatenation and remember to keep the return value of String operations.

equals-hashcode.title: The equals and hashCode contract
equals-hashcode.short: Keep equality and hash codes consistent
equals-hashcode.summary: Keep equality and hash codes consistent. Available on Java 8 and later.
equals-hashcode.why: Objects that are equal according to equals must produce the same hashCode for hash-based collections to work correctly.
equals-hashcode.tips: Whenever you override equals, implement hashCode from the same equality-defining fields as well.

generics.title: Generics basics
generics.summary: Build type-safe collections and APIs. Available on Java 8 and later.
generics.why: Generics move many type errors from runtime casts to compile-time checks.
generics.tips: Avoid raw types and use wildcards at API boundaries when callers need controlled flexibility.

wildcards.title: Wildcards: extends and super
wildcards.short: Express variance at generic API boundaries
wildcards.summary: Express variance at generic API boundaries. Available on Java 8 and later.
wildcards.why: Generic types are invariant by default, so wildcards describe which related element types can safely be read or written.
wildcards.tips: Use PECS: Producer Extends, Consumer Super, and prefer concrete types for return values when possible.

checked-vs-unchecked.title: Checked vs unchecked exceptions
checked-vs-unchecked.short: Understand which exceptions must be handled or declared
checked-vs-unchecked.summary: Understand which exceptions must be handled or declared. Available on Java 8 and later.
checked-vs-unchecked.why: Checked exceptions make failure handling part of the compile-time API contract through catch or throws.
checked-vs-unchecked.tips: Handle failures where recovery is meaningful; otherwise propagate them while preserving the original cause.

optional.title: Represent absence with Optional
optional.short: Represent an optional return value explicitly
optional.summary: Represent an optional return value explicitly. Available on Java 8 and later.
optional.why: Optional can make an absent return value explicit in the type instead of relying on an unchecked null convention.
optional.tips: It is most useful for return values; prefer map, orElseGet, and orElseThrow over calling get blindly.

stream-laziness.title: Streams are lazy
stream-laziness.short: Intermediate operations run only when a terminal operation starts
stream-laziness.summary: Intermediate operations run only when a terminal operation starts. Available on Java 8 and later.
stream-laziness.why: Operations such as filter and map build a pipeline and do not process elements until a terminal operation consumes it.
stream-laziness.tips: Avoid depending on side effects in intermediate operations and check for a terminal operation when nothing appears to run.

static-members.title: Static members
static-members.short: Members that belong to the class rather than an instance
static-members.summary: Members that belong to the class rather than an instance. Available on Java 8 and later.
static-members.why: A static member belongs to the class itself and can be used without a particular object instance.
static-members.tips: Avoid turning shared mutable state into static fields unnecessarily because it complicates tests and concurrency.

pattern-matching-instanceof.title: Pattern matching for instanceof
pattern-matching-instanceof.short: Combine a type test and cast
pattern-matching-instanceof.summary: Combine a type test and cast. Available on Java 16 and later.
pattern-matching-instanceof.why: Pattern matching combines a successful type check with a safely typed variable, eliminating duplicate casts.
pattern-matching-instanceof.tips: The pattern variable's scope depends on control flow, so be careful with negation and compound boolean expressions.

list-basics.title: List basics
list-basics.summary: Create and modify ordered collections. Available on Java 8 and later.
list-basics.why: List is the standard ordered collection abstraction and preserves element order and duplicates.
list-basics.tips: Choose an implementation based on your access and update patterns rather than defaulting blindly to one type.

set-basics.title: Use Set for unique values
set-basics.summary: Work with unique elements. Available on Java 8 and later.
set-basics.why: Set represents uniqueness directly and is useful for deduplication and membership checks.
set-basics.tips: HashSet relies on equals and hashCode; choose a different Set implementation when ordering matters.

map-basics.title: Map basics
map-basics.summary: Store key-value associations. Available on Java 8 and later.
map-basics.why: Map directly models lookup by key and is a foundation for indexes, caches, and counting tasks.
map-basics.tips: If null values are possible, use containsKey when you need to distinguish a missing key from a mapped null.

hashmap-basics.title: Count frequencies with HashMap
hashmap-basics.summary: Count occurrences with Map.merge. Available on Java 8 and later.
hashmap-basics.why: Map.merge combines first insertion and later updates into one operation, which is convenient for frequency counting.
hashmap-basics.tips: Keep key equality stable and compare merge with compute methods when update logic becomes more complex.

stream-map-filter.title: Filter and map a Stream
stream-map-filter.summary: Compose filtering and transformation. Available on Java 8 and later.
stream-map-filter.why: filter and map express selection and transformation as a readable data-processing pipeline.
stream-map-filter.tips: Operation order affects cost and sometimes behavior; filter early when possible and avoid side effects in the pipeline.

stream-to-list.title: Convert a Stream to a List
stream-to-list.summary: Collect stream results with Stream.toList. Available on Java 16 and later.
stream-to-list.why: A terminal collection step turns a lazy Stream pipeline into a concrete List for ordinary downstream code.
stream-to-list.tips: Stream.toList returns an unmodifiable List; use a different collector when the result must be mutable.

files-read-string.title: Read a file as a String
files-read-string.summary: Read text with Files.readString. Available on Java 11 and later.
files-read-string.why: Files.readString provides a concise way to load small text files without manual stream plumbing.
files-read-string.tips: For large files, prefer streaming instead of loading everything into memory, and specify the expected charset.

path-basics.title: Work with file paths using Path
path-basics.short: Build file paths without manual separators
path-basics.summary: Build file paths without manual separators. Available on Java 8 and later.
path-basics.why: Path provides platform-aware path operations without manually concatenating separator characters.
path-basics.tips: Use resolve, normalize, and toAbsolutePath instead of building paths with string concatenation.

httpclient-get.title: Send a GET request with HttpClient
httpclient-get.short: Fetch an HTTP response with the standard HttpClient
httpclient-get.summary: Fetch an HTTP response with the standard HttpClient. Available on Java 11 and later.
httpclient-get.why: The standard HttpClient covers common HTTP requests without requiring a third-party HTTP library.
httpclient-get.tips: Reuse HttpClient instances and define policies for timeouts, status codes, IOException, and InterruptedException.

completable-future.title: Asynchronous pipelines with CompletableFuture
completable-future.summary: Compose asynchronous stages. Available on Java 8 and later.
completable-future.why: CompletableFuture represents an eventual result and lets transformations and combinations be chained without deeply nested callbacks.
completable-future.tips: Know which Executor runs each stage, handle exceptional completion, and avoid accidental blocking with join or get.

executor-service.title: Run tasks with ExecutorService
executor-service.short: Submit work to a thread pool
executor-service.summary: Submit work to a thread pool. Available on Java 8 and later.
executor-service.why: ExecutorService separates task submission from thread creation and manages reusable worker threads for you.
executor-service.tips: Shut an ExecutorService down when finished and choose a pool strategy that matches the workload and blocking behavior.

string-formatting.title: Format strings with String.formatted
string-formatting.summary: Create formatted strings readably. Available on Java 15 and later.
string-formatting.why: Formatting keeps placeholder rules in one readable template instead of scattering string concatenation across the expression.
string-formatting.tips: When numeric or date presentation is locale-sensitive, consider an API that lets you specify Locale explicitly.

null-pointer-exception.title: NullPointerException
null-pointer-exception.short: A member was accessed through null
null-pointer-exception.summary: A member was accessed through null. Available on Java 8 and later.
null-pointer-exception.why: A null reference has no object behind it, so member access, method calls, or array operations cannot proceed.
null-pointer-exception.tips: Start from the first relevant frame in the stack trace and trace backward to where the value became null.

number-format-exception.title: NumberFormatException
number-format-exception.short: A non-numeric string was parsed as a number
number-format-exception.summary: A non-numeric string was parsed as a number. Available on Java 8 and later.
number-format-exception.why: Parsing fails when the input string does not match the numeric format expected by methods such as parseInt.
number-format-exception.tips: Check whitespace, sign, radix, and decimal format, and handle invalid external input explicitly.

index-out-of-bounds.title: IndexOutOfBoundsException
index-out-of-bounds.short: An index was outside the collection bounds
index-out-of-bounds.summary: An index was outside the collection bounds. Available on Java 8 and later.
index-out-of-bounds.why: Valid List indexes range from zero inclusive to size exclusive; anything outside that range has no element.
index-out-of-bounds.tips: Recheck < versus <= and test empty collections and the last valid index as boundary cases.

class-cast-exception.title: ClassCastException
class-cast-exception.short: An object was cast to an incompatible type
class-cast-exception.summary: An object was cast to an incompatible type. Available on Java 8 and later.
class-cast-exception.why: A reference cast fails when the runtime object is not compatible with the requested target type.
class-cast-exception.tips: Prefer better typing or pattern matching with instanceof when the runtime type genuinely needs to be inspected.

concurrent-modification-exception.title: ConcurrentModificationException
concurrent-modification-exception.short: A collection was structurally modified during iteration
concurrent-modification-exception.summary: A collection was structurally modified during iteration. Available on Java 8 and later.
concurrent-modification-exception.why: Many collection iterators are fail-fast and detect structural changes that occur outside the iterator while iteration is in progress.
concurrent-modification-exception.tips: Use Iterator.remove, removeIf, or collect changes separately instead of modifying the collection directly in a for-each loop.

io-exception.title: IOException
io-exception.summary: An I/O operation failed. Available on Java 8 and later.
io-exception.why: File and network operations depend on external resources and can fail because of missing files, permissions, connections, or device errors.
io-exception.tips: Handle the exception where recovery is meaningful; otherwise propagate it while keeping the original cause and context.

unreported-exception.title: Unhandled checked exception
unreported-exception.short: A checked exception is neither caught nor declared
unreported-exception.summary: A checked exception is neither caught nor declared. Available on Java 8 and later.
unreported-exception.why: Calls that can throw checked exceptions require the caller to catch them or declare them with throws.
unreported-exception.tips: Catch only when you can respond meaningfully; otherwise declare an appropriate throws clause and let the caller decide.

non-static-from-static.title: Non-static member from static context
non-static-from-static.short: An instance member was used without an instance
non-static-from-static.summary: An instance member was used without an instance. Available on Java 8 and later.
non-static-from-static.why: A static context has no implicit this object, so it cannot directly access members that belong to a particular instance.
non-static-from-static.tips: Obtain or create the relevant object, or reconsider whether the member truly represents class-level behavior and should be static.

incompatible-types.title: Incompatible types
incompatible-types.short: The source and target types are incompatible
incompatible-types.summary: The source and target types are incompatible. Available on Java 8 and later.
incompatible-types.why: Java's static type checker rejects assignments and arguments when no permitted conversion exists between the source and target types.
incompatible-types.tips: Compare the expected and actual types carefully, including generic type arguments and available conversions.

cannot-find-symbol.title: Cannot find symbol
cannot-find-symbol.short: A referenced name cannot be resolved
cannot-find-symbol.summary: A referenced name cannot be resolved. Available on Java 8 and later.
cannot-find-symbol.why: The compiler cannot resolve the requested variable, type, or method from the current scope, imports, and classpath.
cannot-find-symbol.tips: Check spelling, capitalization, declaration scope, imports, and classpath in that order.

lambda-effectively-final.title: Lambda captures must be effectively final
lambda-effectively-final.short: A lambda tries to mutate a captured local variable
lambda-effectively-final.summary: A lambda tries to mutate a captured local variable. Available on Java 8 and later.
lambda-effectively-final.why: Local variables captured by a lambda must be final or effectively final so the captured value has stable semantics.
lambda-effectively-final.tips: For aggregation, prefer Stream reduce or collect, or redesign the state flow instead of mutating a captured local variable.

unchecked-cast-warning.title: Unchecked cast warning
unchecked-cast-warning.short: A generic cast cannot be fully checked at runtime
unchecked-cast-warning.summary: A generic cast cannot be fully checked at runtime. Available on Java 8 and later.
unchecked-cast-warning.why: Type erasure means the runtime often cannot verify generic arguments such as the String in List<String>.
unchecked-cast-warning.tips: Fix the raw or weakly typed source where possible and suppress the warning only in the smallest region whose safety you can prove.

rawtypes-warning.title: Raw type warning
rawtypes-warning.short: A generic type is used without type arguments
rawtypes-warning.summary: A generic type is used without type arguments. Available on Java 8 and later.
rawtypes-warning.why: Raw types bypass part of generic type checking and can defer mistakes until a ClassCastException at runtime.
rawtypes-warning.tips: Write List<String> rather than List and isolate unavoidable legacy raw APIs at a narrow boundary.

deprecation-warning.title: Deprecation warning
deprecation-warning.summary: Code uses an API marked @Deprecated. Available on Java 8 and later.
deprecation-warning.why: Deprecation signals that an API may have a safer replacement, compatibility concerns, or a future removal path.
deprecation-warning.tips: Read the Javadoc deprecation note and migration guidance before suppressing the warning or continuing to depend on the API.

string-equals-not-reference.title: Using == for String comparison
string-equals-not-reference.short: Reference identity is used when value equality was intended
string-equals-not-reference.summary: Reference identity is used when value equality was intended. Available on Java 8 and later.
string-equals-not-reference.why: For reference types, == checks whether both references point to the same object, not whether two String values contain the same text.
string-equals-not-reference.tips: Use equals for String contents, or Objects.equals when either side may be null.

mutable-hashmap-key.title: Mutating a HashMap key
mutable-hashmap-key.short: A key is mutated after insertion into a hash-based map
mutable-hashmap-key.summary: A key is mutated after insertion into a hash-based map. Available on Java 8 and later.
mutable-hashmap-key.why: Changing fields used by equals or hashCode can move the logical key away from the bucket where HashMap originally stored it.
mutable-hashmap-key.tips: Prefer immutable keys and never mutate equality-defining state while an object is being used as a hash key.

optional-get-without-check.title: Calling Optional.get blindly
optional-get-without-check.short: A value is read without handling the empty case
optional-get-without-check.summary: A value is read without handling the empty case. Available on Java 8 and later.
optional-get-without-check.why: Calling get on an empty Optional throws NoSuchElementException and defeats the purpose of making absence explicit.
optional-get-without-check.tips: Use map, ifPresent, orElseGet, orElseThrow, or another API that expresses what the empty case should mean.

stream-reuse.title: Reusing a Stream
stream-reuse.short: A stream is reused after a terminal operation
stream-reuse.summary: A stream is reused after a terminal operation. Available on Java 8 and later.
stream-reuse.why: A Stream is a single-use pipeline and is considered consumed after a terminal operation runs.
stream-reuse.tips: Create a fresh Stream from the source each time, or use a Supplier<Stream<T>> when repeated traversal is intentional.

integer-division.title: Integer division truncates
integer-division.short: Integer operands are divided before assignment to double
integer-division.summary: Integer operands are divided before assignment to double. Available on Java 8 and later.
integer-division.why: The operation is chosen from the operand types, so int divided by int performs integer division before any later double assignment.
integer-division.tips: Convert one operand to double before dividing when you need a fractional result, and consider rounding behavior explicitly.

shared-mutable-state.title: Shared mutable state in concurrency
shared-mutable-state.short: Multiple threads mutate shared state without coordination
shared-mutable-state.summary: Multiple threads mutate shared state without coordination. Available on Java 8 and later.
shared-mutable-state.why: Unsynchronized reads and writes can race, causing lost updates and visibility problems between threads.
shared-mutable-state.tips: Reduce shared state first; when sharing is required, choose synchronized, Lock, atomic classes, or concurrent collections deliberately.
